_note: Operation-level risk escalation data for the backend. The MCP server does NOT read this; it is policy the backend owns. Baseline per-tool risk comes from list_tools (_meta.reconix.risk). This file lists, per tool, the operations (flags/subcommands) that push a call ABOVE that tool's baseline.
match: For a call, lowercase its argument VALUES, join with spaces, and substring-test each pattern listed under that call's tool. A call's risk = max(tool baseline, highest tier whose pattern matches). Patterns are conservative; a match on a legit value (e.g. a target literally named 'exploit') is a rare, safe-side false positive. Extend per engagement.

per_tool._comment: Escalations defined per tool (no global block). Only tools whose baseline (medium/low) can actually jump are listed; the 14 already-high tools are omitted because the backend gates them at baseline, so any pattern on them is a no-op under max(). This also drops the former global-medium patterns, which only owned already-medium tools and so could never escalate.

nmap._comment: Baseline is low (a plain port/service scan). These raise a call above that: medium for intrusive-but-safe options, high for offensive NSE categories.
